executive_summary: EUR/AUD trades at 1.63673 (5 August close), essentially unchanged over one month (−0.06%), up 0.82% over three months, down 2.31% over six months and down 7.44% over twelve — a year in which the Australian dollar comprehensively outperformed the euro and drove the pair from a 1.8162 high (17 October 2025) to a 1.6111 low (13 May 2026). Spot now sits at the 12th percentile of its 52-week range, which is the single most important framing fact in this report: the pair has already fully priced the RBA's ascent to the highest policy rate in the G10+SGD complex and the euro area's absorption of an adverse energy shock. The dominant bilateral narrative is a −210bp policy differential (ECB deposit 2.25% versus RBA cash 4.35%) that is about to begin narrowing for the first time in three years, because the ECB carries a 77–83% probability of hiking on 10 September while the RBA's 29 July CPI undershoot cut its 11 August hike odds to roughly a coin flip and pushed CBA, NAB and ANZ to forecast no further 2026 move. Three bilateral differentials diverge sharply from what either standalone dossier implies: first, speculators are simultaneously at a sample-extreme short in EUR (leveraged funds −56,671 contracts, 0th percentile, extending to −65,198 on the 28 July report) and net long AUD (+24,788), which makes the pair-implied speculative position maximally short EUR/AUD — an amplified, not muted, positioning signal; second, the commodity netting is double-geared rather than offsetting, because every energy tick that taxes the euro area's terms of trade simultaneously subsidises Australia's, making EUR/AUD the cleanest short-energy expression in the G10; third, both dossiers independently compute a relative-REER fair value of 1.7360–1.7362, leaving spot 5.7% cheap against a 97th-percentile Australian real exchange rate. We are tactically Neutral at conviction 2 (weighted score +0.0492), because the −210bp carry drag, a benign risk regime that favours the higher-beta quote currency, and a live two-way 11 August RBA binary genuinely offset an improving euro data pulse and a crowded pair-implied short. We are strategically Bullish at conviction 2 (weighted score +0.1556) with a 1.6750 six-month target, 236 pips above the 1.6514 six-month forward outright and roughly 500 pips above the retrievable model-forecast consensus — the caveat being that the euro's own external balance and the 17 November French budget vote are the two live routes to being wrong.

market_context.valuation_assessment: Both dossiers compute the same relative-REER conclusion independently, which is unusual and raises confidence in it. The EUR dossier puts the euro 5.9% cheap versus the Australian dollar on relative deviation from 30-month REER means, with an implied fair value of EUR/AUD 1.7362; the AUD dossier puts the Australian dollar 5.89% rich versus the euro with an implied fair value of EUR/AUD 1.7360. Spot at 1.63673 is therefore 5.7% below the mid-point of those two independent estimates. Australia's BIS real broad effective exchange rate printed 115.92 in June 2026, up 9.8% year-on-year, 6.4% above its 30-month mean and at the 97th percentile of the available window. The euro area's REER printed 102.69, down 1.2% year-on-year and only 0.5% above its own 30-month mean, at roughly the 55th percentile. EUR/AUD is the one euro cross in which valuation is unambiguously a tailwind. The caveat is methodological: both figures are deviations from a 30-month mean, not absolute PPP estimates, and REER extremes persist for quarters, so this is a strategic anchor and not a tactical trigger. What the current level prices is a permanent 210bp Australian carry advantage, a permanent energy-driven Australian terms-of-trade windfall, and a euro area that never repairs its external position — the first of those three is already being falsified.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime since mid-July has been a coil that resolved sharply higher on one session and then stalled. From 1.64517 on 13 July the pair ground down to 1.62638 on 27 July, printing a higher low at 1.62360 on 26 July, before rallying 0.98% in a single session on 29 July to close 1.64871 — the day Australian June-quarter CPI undershot at 3.8% headline with trimmed mean flat at 3.6%. The move extended as the euro area delivered a Q2 GDP beat (+0.4% q/q vs 0.2% consensus) on 30 July and a July flash HICP accelerating on all four components to 2.9% headline/2.5% core on 31 July. Since then the pair has consolidated in a 1.6359-1.6504 band, closing at 1.63673. The dominant narrative is a simultaneous, opposite-signed inflation inflection in the two economies, exactly the configuration that reverses a carry-driven downtrend, which the market has so far priced by only about one big figure.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_regime: carry not compensating / carry working against the pair
bilateral_carry_analysis.breakeven_move: A long EUR/AUD position must appreciate 28 pips per month to offset carry, and 171 pips over six months, before losing money; a carry-collecting short can absorb a 171-pip adverse move over six months (to 1.6514) before losing money
bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The annualised carry for a long EUR/AUD position is -210bp, the largest absolute carry penalty the euro faces against any G10 currency. Carry-to-vol for the short is +0.41 against 5.1-5.2% realised vol, one of the better risk-adjusted carry trades in the complex, better than short EUR/USD (-0.24) or long AUD/USD (+0.10). Tradeable carry in forwards is narrower than the headline, at 163-195bp via Euribor vs the Australian bill/note curve. Carry regime assessment is that carry is working, and it is working against the pair: the two best-performing euro crosses over twelve months are EUR/NOK and EUR/AUD, both out-carried by 200bp or more, and realised volatility of 5.1-5.2% is exactly the range in which carry compounds rather than gets stopped out. The forward curve prices 0.90% of euro appreciation over six months purely as carry mechanics, with the annualised premium declining across tenors (2.14% to 1.80%), meaning the convergence trade is already partly priced; our edge is expecting more convergence than the curve embeds, via both legs.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The differential is −210bp against the pair and it is the largest single obstacle to any long EUR/AUD position: the ECB deposit rate of 2.25% ranks eighth of eleven in the G10+SGD policy ranking while the RBA's 4.35% ranks first, and the euro is out-carried by more here than against any other G10 currency. The trajectory, however, has inflected for the first time in three years and it has inflected in the pair's favour: the ECB carries a 76.9–83% market-implied probability of a 25bp hike on 10 September and a 91.9% cumulative probability of a deposit rate above 2.25% by 17 December, while the RBA's 11 August hike probability collapsed from above 90% to roughly 50% after the 29 July CPI undershoot, with CBA, NAB and ANZ all now forecasting no further 2026 move and only Westpac holding out for August. If the ECB delivers on 10 September and the RBA holds on 11 August, the differential narrows from 210bp to 185bp inside five weeks — worth roughly 1.0–1.5% of pair appreciation on the twelve-month beta. Against that, the Australian front end is not yet agreeing with the 'RBA is done' view: the 2-year ACGB at 4.57% sits 22bp above cash and the 52-week note at 4.59% sits 24bp above, still pricing close to one full further hike, so an 11 August hike is a genuine 50% risk that would re-widen the differential to 235bp and take the pair straight back toward 1.6200. Term structure reinforces the drag but not the direction: the Bund at 3.15% yields 178bp less than the ACGB 10-year at 4.93%, and the German 2-year at 2.76% yields 181bp less than the Australian 2-year. Transmission for this pair is unusually direct because neither leg has a dollar to mediate it: relative rate expectations move EUR/AUD one-for-one through the forward curve. The honest tactical read is that the level of carry and the improving trajectory are close to balanced across a four-week window that contains one live 50/50 binary, which is what a genuine Neutral looks like.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential arithmetic is the strongest bullish argument this pair has, and it runs in only one direction. The ECB has one hike delivered, a 77–83% probability of a second on 10 September and a 91.9% cumulative probability of being above 2.25% by 17 December, with a real policy rate of −0.65% that leaves it further behind its own inflation than any peer. The RBA, by contrast, has a real policy rate of +0.55% — a 120bp real-rate gap in Australia's favour that is precisely why the pair is where it is, and precisely the gap that closes if the ECB hikes twice while Australian inflation continues decelerating. The base case is 210bp → 185bp by mid-September and → 160bp by February 2027 if the ECB reaches 2.75% and the RBA holds; the tail case, in which CBA's forecast of two 2027 Australian cuts starts being priced, takes the implied 2027 differential toward 110–135bp. A 50bp realised compression is worth roughly 2.0–3.0% of pair appreciation, and the 2027 repricing is worth more. Crucially, this compression does not require the Fed to do anything, distinguishing it from the euro's consensus bull case against the dollar. The counterweight is that the starting deficit is enormous and the euro will still be out-carried by 160bp at the end of the horizon, so a long position pays 171 pips of carry over six months; the forward curve already embeds part of the convergence via a declining annualised premium. Confidence at 56 rather than higher reflects that the Australian 52-week note still prices one more hike and the RBA has an explicit, repeated tightening bias honoured three times in 2026.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral surprise differential inflected in the pair's favour within a 72-hour window at the end of July, and this is the cleanest tactical signal in the report. Australia's June-quarter CPI on 29 July printed 3.8% headline against 4.0% consensus with the trimmed mean flat at 3.6%, breaking a sequence that had run 4.6% in March, 4.2% in April and 4.0% in May; the euro area's July flash on 31 July printed 2.9% headline against 2.8%, core 2.5% against 2.4%, services 3.3% against 3.2% and energy 10.0% against 8.5% - four of four accelerating. On the same days the euro area beat on growth (Q2 GDP +0.4% q/q against 0.2% consensus) while Australia's most recent quarterly print was +0.3%. The inflation level still favours the Australian dollar by 90bp headline and 110bp core, but the direction has flipped, and it is direction that moves the relative policy curve inside four weeks. Leading indicators reinforce the asymmetry: euro-area composite PMI rose to a five-month high of 51.9, German ifo rose a third consecutive month to 86.6, ZEW German expectations leapt 15.8 points to +26.3 - while Australia's Westpac-Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment at 83.9 sits in the bottom decile of a fifty-year history and NAB business confidence at -5 sits in the bottom decile since 1997. Transmission for this pair runs through the relative-hike-probability channel with double-geared exposure. That is why 29 July produced a 0.98% single-session rally, the pair's largest up-day of the quarter.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the same data reads as a standoff, because the composition of each economy's inflation undermines the other's apparent advantage. The euro area's acceleration is almost entirely cost-push: ex-energy HICP is 2.2% and unchanged from June, the ECB's wage tracker sits at 2.3% for 2026, and Lagarde has stated second-round effects are not visible - the impulse mechanically self-liquidates during 2027. Australia's disinflation is equally suspect in composition: the headline decline was driven by automotive fuel falling 10.9% in the month, which the ABS excludes from the trimmed mean every month since March 2026, while electricity at +22.4% is a rebate-rolloff and new dwellings at +5.8% is genuine cost pass-through. So the euro area's inflation is real but temporary and Australia's disinflation is partly cosmetic - the two errors point in opposite directions and roughly cancel. Growth is equally balanced: Australia's 2.5% year-on-year comfortably exceeds the euro area's 1.0%, but Australia's quarterly momentum is 0.3% against the euro area's 0.4% and Australia's leading indicators are in the bottom decile while the euro area's are at five-month highs. The one genuinely asymmetric observation is labour markets: Australian unemployment is 4.4% with employment up 76,300 in June, whereas euro-area unemployment has been flat at 6.3% since March. A firm Australian labour market keeps the RBA's tightening option alive and is the principal route by which this factor turns against the pair. Genuinely Neutral, and at only a 0.10 strategic weight it costs little either way.

Strategically what matters is persistence, and there the two economies' compositional flaws cancel: the euro area's energy impulse is self-liquidating without wages, while Australia's disinflation is partly a fuel effect its own central bank excludes from the target measure. Confidence falls from 60 to 50 because the tactical judgement rests on observed prints and the strategic one on a forecast of wage and energy behaviour in both economies simultaneously.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: EUR/AUD is a moderate-to-high inverse risk-sensitivity pair - risk-on drives the pair lower, risk-off drives it higher - and the current regime is squarely risk-on. The Australian dollar is the G10's highest-beta currency to global risk appetite in both directions, while the euro at a 2.25% deposit rate is one of the three cheapest funding currencies in the bloc. A benign risk environment simultaneously bids the quote currency and finances shorts in the base currency - the pair falls twice for one reason. The observable metrics are all supportive: VIX 17.09, US IG OAS 81bp, US HY OAS 281bp, S&P 500 near 7,467, STOXX Europe 600 at a record 655.45 and LME copper near US$14,195/t, up roughly 46% year-on-year at a 2026 record. European equities made record highs in July and the euro captured only 1.36% of it against the dollar - a realised beta well under one - precisely because the funding-currency drag offsets the anti-dollar bid, and the CFTC data confirm it, with leveraged funds building a sample-extreme euro short during the same month European equities set records. The correlation regime is intact rather than broken, and there is no dated catalyst inside four weeks that reliably breaks it. State Street's custody data show global institutions ended H1 2026 with equity allocations at two-decade highs and the Risk Appetite Index climbing to 0.45 in June from 0.09 in April, alongside renewed appetite for the Australian dollar.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the inverse gearing that currently pushes the pair down becomes the strongest reason to own it, because the distribution around a 17 VIX is one-sided for this specific cross. The quote currency has the most negative convexity in the G10, and the base currency is the funding leg that gets bought back when carry-trade unwinds occur. In a genuine risk-off event EUR/AUD does not merely stop falling; it gaps higher, because carry-trade unwinds and funding-currency repurchases are the same transaction. As of end-2024, 48% of Australian superannuation assets were held internationally, historically only 20-30% of offshore equity portfolios were hedged - a A$4.3 trillion pool with an 80% unhedged offshore book must sell AUD to re-establish hedges in a drawdown, and a material share of that offshore book is European. That is a pro-cyclical, one-directional EUR/AUD-buying flow that activates in exactly the scenario where the pair's fundamentals also turn. Set against this, the risk regime could simply persist - copper at a record and credit at cycle tights have persisted for five months through a chokepoint closure - and if it does, the pair keeps grinding lower. We resolve Bullish at 55 because the payoff is convex rather than because the base case has changed.

CFTC leveraged funds were net short 56,671 EURO FX contracts in the 21 July report - the 0th percentile of a 25-week range - extending to a net short 65,198 in the 28 July report, while leveraged funds were net long 24,788 AUD contracts. Net, inside four weeks the fast flow sets the price and the fast flow is wrong-footed in both legs of this cross.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a one-to-six-month horizon positioning inverts its own signal for both legs simultaneously, which is why this factor scores Neutral. A 0th-percentile leveraged euro short is a powerful two-week catalyst and a meaningless six-month one - by definition it cannot get more extreme and will be flat or reversed long before the horizon closes - while a 50th-percentile Australian long offers no contrarian content at all. What survives is the real-money configuration, and there the picture is a headwind for the pair: euro asset managers are long 228,927 contracts and reducing at ~26,000 per four weeks, while Australian asset managers are short 35,144 and covering. Structural bilateral flows, however, cut the other way and are not visible in futures data. The Kangaroo market recorded ~A$191.74bn of issuance in H1 2026, ~42% higher than H1 2025, with six overseas borrowers completing inaugural AUD offerings including Commerzbank and CaixaBank. European issuers raising AUD and swapping proceeds into euros are a mechanical, recurring EUR/AUD-supportive flow, and at a record A$52bn in a half-year it is material. Second, the superannuation hedging channel described in Factor 3 is a contingent, pro-cyclical EUR/AUD buyer. These structural flows roughly offset the real-money overhang. Neutral.

Two secondary migrations reinforce it: Factors 3 and 10 flip from Bearish to Bullish as the observable-metrics story gives way to the distributional story, and Factor 2 falls from Bullish to Neutral as the July surprise differential decays, removing +0.1080 - the largest single loss - which is why the strategic score is only 0.106 higher despite Factor 1's +0.1344 gain.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The window between 11 August (RBA decision plus SoMP) and 10 September (ECB decision plus staff projections in Berlin), with secondary confirmation at 28 October (Australian Q3 CPI) and 3 November (RBA November SoMP)
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Do not run a tactical long into 11 August - the base-case risk/reward of 0.32:1 gross and the 28-pip monthly carry make an open-ended spot long a losing modal proposition. The correct sequencing is to wait for the RBA, then establish the strategic position either on confirmation (a close above 1.6520 for three sessions) or on a hold of 1.6248-1.6371, and to express it in the six-month forward at 1.65142 rather than in spot so the carry is embedded rather than paid. Size must be reduced into the 10-17 November window.

catalysts.event: RBA Monetary Policy Board decision + August Statement on Monetary Policy + Governor's press conference
catalysts.rationale: The dominant event of the tactical window and a genuine 50/50 binary after the 29 July CPI undershoot. A 25bp hike to 4.60% re-widens the differential from 210bp to 235bp and takes the pair straight to 1.6250; a hold that retains the tightening clause leaves the pair near spot; a hold that softens or removes the clause unwinds the 52-week note's 24bp premium and gaps the pair through 1.6492.

June showed unemployment steady at 4.4% with employment up 76,300, and a firm labour market is the principal reason the RBA's tightening option remains alive. A rise above 4.6% would confirm 75bp of 2026 tightening is finally biting and effectively end the Australian hiking cycle, bullish for the pair by roughly 60-80 pips; a print below 4.3% with strong full-time gains reinstates the September hike risk.

catalysts.event: Publication of the ECB Account of the 23 July monetary policy meeting
catalysts.rationale: Lagarde disclosed some governors asked whether a hike should be considered, and the Account will document how many and how forcefully. A hawkish July Account would push September pricing from 77-83% toward 90% and compress the differential expectation before the RBA's next meeting.

catalysts.event: Fitch scheduled sovereign rating review of France
catalysts.rationale: Fitch downgraded France to A+ in September 2025 with a Stable outlook. With a 5.1% deficit, 117.5% debt and a Bercy report warning of 5.9% by 2027, an outlook move to Negative is live and would take OAT-Bund from 82bp toward 95-100bp, with no offsetting quote-currency vulnerability given Australia's triple-A curve.

catalysts.event: Eurostat euro-area flash HICP for August 2026
catalysts.rationale: The decisive input for the 10 September ECB decision, doubly important because it arrives after Australian CPI has already decelerated for four consecutive months. A print at or above 2.9% locks in the September hike; a print at or below 2.6% cuts September odds below 55% and voids the tactical case. We expect 2.9-3.1%.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision plus staff macroeconomic projections, Berlin
catalysts.rationale: The single most important dated event for the base leg. A 25bp hike to 2.50% is 77-83% priced (partial sell-the-fact), but the projections carry larger information content: an upward revision to 2026 HICP toward 3.2% with 2027 held at or above 2.3% forces the curve higher and takes the differential to 185bp with a path toward 160bp.
catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the hike; not at all for the projection revisions

catalysts.event: FOMC decision plus Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The first full SEP since forward guidance was removed, and the clearest read yet on a Fed that held 9-3 in July with three dissents for a hike. A hawkish SEP compresses the Australia-US policy gap from +72.5bp to roughly +35bp and pushes the dollar toward the leg of the smile where high-beta currencies underperform, hurting the quote leg more than the base leg.

catalysts.event: German state elections, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin
catalysts.rationale: The highest-salience German political event of the autumn, arriving ten days after the ECB and four days after the FOMC. A strong AfD result would pressure the Merz coalition at the moment it is passing a 2027 draft budget carrying €109.7bn of defence spending, raising questions about the German fiscal expansion underpinning Bund yields and the base leg's rate story.

catalysts.event: RBA Monetary Policy Board decision (no SoMP)
catalysts.rationale: Lower information content without a forecast round, but falls immediately after the ECB and FOMC and will be read as a relative-policy event. If the ECB has hiked and the RBA holds, the compression thesis gains its first concrete confirmation and the pair should extend through 1.6520; a surprise hike here would be more damaging than one on 11 August.

catalysts.event: China Q3 2026 GDP and September activity data
catalysts.rationale: The single highest-beta non-domestic release for the quote leg and near-irrelevant for the base leg. China takes approximately 30% of Australian exports, Q2 GDP was 4.3% (weakest since Q4 2022), and the July NBS manufacturing PMI fell back into contraction at 49.2. A sub-4.0% print would force a downgrade to Australian bulk volumes on top of an iron ore price already down 8% year-to-date.

catalysts.event: ABS Consumer Price Index, September quarter 2026
catalysts.rationale: The highest-impact Australian domestic release of the horizon because of the quarterly cadence. June showed 3.8% headline with the trimmed mean flat at 3.6%. A trimmed mean at or below 3.4% removes the last hike from the Australian curve and takes the differential toward 160bp; a re-acceleration above 3.9% revives the tightening cycle and re-widens the gap.

catalysts.event: RBA decision plus November Statement on Monetary Policy
catalysts.rationale: The second forecast round of the horizon and the first RBA document to confront a materially compressed relative-rate position, with the ECB having hiked in September and possibly signalling December. It is also the first plausible venue for an Australian easing bias to appear in the Bank's own forecasts, which CBA already forecasts for 2027.

A dated, binary trade-policy event that transmits to the Australian dollar faster and harder than to any other G10 currency, because AUD is the most liquid China proxy in the complex. Falls eight days before the French budget vote, so the two November binaries partly hedge each other within the position.

catalysts.event: French Assemblee nationale solemn vote on the PLF 2027 as a whole
catalysts.rationale: The largest single identified downside binary for this pair. A successful censure motion means dissolution and snap legislative elections weeks before a presidential campaign in which Bardella polls at 35%. We put that path at 20-25% and estimate it takes OAT-Bund from 82bp through 130bp, historically dragging the euro 1.0-1.5% lower trade-weighted independent of the ECB, with no offsetting quote-currency vulnerability.

catalysts.event: ECB decision plus Eurosystem staff projections
catalysts.rationale: The market prices a 91.9% cumulative probability of a deposit rate above 2.25% by this date, and the projection round is the first to extend meaningfully into 2029. If the ECB reaches 2.75% here while the RBA has held since May, the differential closes to 160bp, worth 2.0-3.0% of appreciation on the pair's twelve-month beta.

catalysts.event: Australian Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook (MYEFO)
catalysts.rationale: The first fiscal update to incorporate commodity realisations running 91-114% above the May Budget assumptions, implying resource company tax receipts well above Budget parameters. For this pair the transmission is via the relative-fiscal-quality channel, partially offsetting the French autumn.

catalysts.event: Full EU ban on Russian LNG imports takes effect
catalysts.rationale: The pair's single worst structural event and the clearest illustration of its double gearing. A self-imposed European supply cut landing alongside constrained Hormuz transit and low EU storage would spike TTF and JKM together, simultaneously taxing the base currency's terms of trade and subsidising the quote currency's LNG export earnings. Unlike most catalysts, there is no offsetting leg.

invalidators.condition: RBA raises the cash rate to 4.60% on 11 August 2026 while ECB September pricing simultaneously falls below 60%
invalidators.mechanism: The ECB-RBA differential would re-widen from 210bp to 235bp, reversing the single mechanism supplying 47% of the strategic score's gross positive; the pair would revert to the carry-driven downtrend that produced a 7.44% twelve-month decline, with 1.6111 back in play
invalidators.monitor_indicator: RBA cash rate target and Central Bank Watch ECB September probability

invalidators.condition: Dutch TTF front-month sustains above €75/MWh for ten consecutive business days while JKM LNG holds above US$25/mmBtu
invalidators.mechanism: This is the only event class that hits both legs of this pair in the same direction - a European terms-of-trade tax and an Australian export windfall from one input - and the pair's energy transmission coefficient is roughly double that of a normal cross, making the combined move worth 250-400 pips
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ICE Dutch TTF front-month settlement and Platts JKM

invalidators.condition: EUR/AUD closes below 1.6111 (the 13 May 2026 52-week low) on a daily basis
invalidators.mechanism: Breaks a four-instance higher-low sequence that is the structural foundation of the strategic case, opening the 1.5913 61.8% retracement of 1.4281-1.8554

invalidators.condition: Australian trimmed-mean CPI on 28 October 2026 re-accelerates to 3.9% or above while euro-area core HICP falls below 2.3%
invalidators.mechanism: The core inflation gap would widen from 110bp back toward 160bp and the real policy rate gap from 120bp toward 170bp, restoring the RBA's tightening option and removing the ECB's - the exact configuration that drove the pair to the 12th percentile of its range
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ABS quarterly CPI trimmed mean and Eurostat HICPX

invalidators.condition: A censure motion against the French government succeeds on or around the 17 November PLF 2027 solemn vote, or OAT-Bund closes above 110bp on any date
invalidators.mechanism: Dissolution weeks before a presidential campaign would revive a redenomination premium against a quote currency that is triple-A with no credit premium at any ACGB tenor - the fiscal asymmetry in this pair is roughly six notches and there is no offsetting Australian vulnerability inside the horizon
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Assemblee nationale censure votes and the OAT-Bund 10Y spread
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily for the spread, per vote for motions

invalidators.condition: China's Q3 2026 GDP prints below 4.0% year-on-year with iron ore 62% Fe CFR China below US$85/t sustained for ten sessions
invalidators.mechanism: The cleanest available asymmetric input for this pair - near-irrelevant for the base leg and existential for a quote currency whose largest single export is forecast to fall from A$117bn to A$108bn against Chinese steel output already down 3.0% in H1
invalidators.monitor_indicator: NBS quarterly GDP and iron ore spot

invalidators.condition: EUR/AUD closes above 1.6842 on a weekly basis
invalidators.mechanism: Invalidates the technical bear case running from the 2025 high, confirming a transition from a stalling downtrend to a reversal, triggering mechanical trend-following inflows from a compressed moving-average cluster

assumptions: Spot is taken as 1.63673, the 5 August 2026 close from the supplied Twelve Data series, notwithstanding a stated valuation date of 1 August 2026 - a five-session gap disclosed rather than adjusted for, since the price series is the designated source of truth for all price-derived metrics

Cross-referencing the two dossiers, the EUR dossier carries EUR/AUD 1.63945 and the AUD dossier 1.6394 at the 31 July close, while the price series gives 1.64080 for the same date; the 13.5-pip discrepancy reflects differing closing conventions and does not change any stance
Twenty-day realised volatility of approximately 5.2% annualised was computed directly from the supplied daily closes and corroborated by the AUD dossier's independent 60-day figure of 5.10%

EUR/AUD OTC 1-month and 3-month at-the-money implied volatility, and the 25-delta risk reversal, could not be sourced from any free public venue; the EUR dossier's estimated 8.0 3-month implied is treated as an implausible upper bound and an inferred 1-month implied of 6.0-6.5 and 3-month of 6.5-7.0 is used, labelled as inference

The near-flat skew for the cross is an inference derived from the observation that both legs carry negative risk reversals against the dollar, which largely cancel in a cross; no direct EUR/AUD skew observation exists

Forward points are CIP-derived, not traded quotes, computed from Euribor fixings against an Australian short-rate curve interpolated between the cash rate and the 52-week note, and exclude the cross-currency basis, which is itself unobservable for EUR/AUD

The relative-REER fair value of 1.7360-1.7362 is a relative misalignment measure anchored on 30-month means, not an absolute PPP calculation, and should be read as a strategic anchor rather than a tactical trigger

Bilateral goods trade is taken directly from the injected IMF DOTS block for 2024 and is not re-estimated from the web; the $25.5bn net goods surplus is converted to a ~$2.1bn monthly flow on a simple twelve-month division, ignoring seasonality

Weight adjustments total ±0.04 on Factor 10, +0.03 on Factor 3 strategically, +0.02 on Factor 5 tactically and +0.01 on Factors 4, 5 and 9, all inside the ±0.05 per-factor limit, with both horizons summing to exactly 1.00

CFTC figures for the 21 July report are carried from both dossiers' cycle extracts; the newer 28 July euro print (-65,198) is disclosed because it strengthens rather than weakens the Factor 4 contrarian case, while the 21 July figures are retained as the primary cross-dossier reference

The retrievable forecast set for this pair is dominated by statistical and model-based publishers rather than bank research desks, with NAB the only named bank retrieved, so divergence magnitude should be discounted accordingly
